item.title: chore(lots): claim wave 3 (LOT-048, 047)
item.body:
Not a lot: orchestrator claim PR. Claims for Mac child sessions: LOT-048 post-form engine (Opus → Fable, deps 036/037/042 done) and LOT-047 MP unread poll (Sonnet → Opus, deps 023/045 done). Owners `mac/w3-<lot>-<model> (2026-10-27)`. LOT-038 was dropped from this claim: its author stopped on LESSONS 35 (no capture of the MPStorage thread page / edit form, no legacy oracle); the capture is added to the Capture backlog (Mac) and 038 stays `blocked`. Wave plan updated. Only `docs/LOTS.md`; check-lot-deps and markdownlint pass.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Restore the required unowned `todo` state before claiming these lots.** The base rows are unowned and `blocked`, but this change sets both owners and marks both lots `in-progress` directly. `AGENTS.md:90` requires a lot to be `todo`, with dependencies and inputs available, and have no owner before it is claimed. This bypasses the claim gate and makes the tracker report active ownership from an invalid starting state.
Suggested fix ```diff -| mac/w3-047-sonnet (2026-10-27) · old [#75](https://github.com/francoisgn/ios-app_SwiftHFR/issues/75) | in-progress | +| — | todo | -| mac/w3-048-opus (2026-10-27) · old [#76](https://github.com/francoisgn/ios-app_SwiftHFR/issues/76) | in-progress | +| — | todo | ```

🧩 Analysis chain
🏁 Script executed: ```shell #!/bin/bash rg -n -C5 'todo|claim|resolv|thread|before.*code|ready' AGENTS.md ``` Length of output: 17171 ---
`@francoisgn` Understood. `docs/LOTS.md` lists all dependencies of LOT-047 and LOT-048 as `done`, and you confirmed that their inputs exist. I withdraw the request for a separate `todo` PR. I treated the stale `blocked` labels as proof that the lots were not claimable. `AGENTS.md` requires readiness and no existing owner, but it does not explicitly require a separate status-only PR. The claim-before-code requirement still applies: the claim PR must merge before writing code, not merely before marking a code PR ready. ✅ Review thread resolved. You are interacting with an AI system.
